articles.headline: Google to invest $15 billion in AI infrastructure and buy nuclear power in Finland
articles.summary: Google’s planned infrastructure spend and energy deal point to continued hyperscaler demand for compute, cooling and power. For businesses, this signals that AI capacity expansion remains capital-intensive and that cloud and energy costs may stay elevated, especially for firms relying on large-scale model training or inference.

articles.headline: Smartphones are going to cost more as the AI boom pushes inflation
articles.summary: Rising costs tied to the AI build-out are flowing through to consumer hardware pricing. That matters for companies that refresh fleets of phones, tablets, and edge devices, because procurement budgets may need to absorb higher device prices and longer replacement cycles.

articles.headline: Mistral raises 3 billion euros in Series D led by Samsung Electronics
articles.summary: The funding round strengthens one of Europe’s leading AI model companies and signals continued competitive investment in frontier AI. For businesses, this may expand model choice, but it also underscores that enterprise AI suppliers are still burning significant capital and racing to scale.
